evidence.title: TLC (TV series)
evidence.text: TLC is a darkly surreal farce-like sitcom set in a fictional NHS hospital called South Middlesex.

evidence.title: TLC (TV series)
evidence.text: Written by Fintan Coyle, co-creator of hit game show "Weakest Link", it was first broadcast on the BBC on 11 November 2002 and ran over six episodes until 16 December.

evidence.title: TLC (TV series)
evidence.text: There were some very mixed opinions on the show among both critics and viewers, but it achieved decent ratings and featured an excellent comedy cast including Richard Griffiths, Alexander Armstrong and "The League of Gentlemen's" Reece Shearsmith.

evidence.title: TLC (TV series)
evidence.text: The series was released on DVD in the UK on 29 October 2007.

evidence.title: Alexander Armstrong's Big Ask
evidence.text: Alexander Armstrong's Big Ask is a British comedy panel show hosted by Alexander Armstrong.

evidence.title: Alexander Armstrong's Big Ask
evidence.text: The pilot was shown on Dave on 30 May 2011.

evidence.title: Alexander Armstrong's Big Ask
evidence.text: The guests on the pilot were Robert Webb, Katy Brand and Griff Rhys Jones.

evidence.title: Alexander Armstrong's Big Ask

evidence.title: Armstrong and Miller
evidence.text: Armstrong and Miller are an English stand-up comedy double act consisting of the actor-comedians Alexander Armstrong and Ben Miller.

evidence.title: Armstrong and Miller
evidence.text: They have performed in two eponymous television sketch shows, the satirical "Timeghost" podcast, and many individual television appearances.

evidence.title: Don't Ask Me Ask Britain
evidence.text: Don't Ask Me Ask Britain is a British television comedy panel game show that has aired on ITV since 18 April 2017 and is hosted by Alexander Armstrong with Frank Skinner and Jonathan Ross as the team captains.

evidence.title: Don't Ask Me Ask Britain
evidence.text: The series is produced by Chalkboard TV for ITV.

evidence.title: Don't Ask Me Ask Britain
evidence.text: The goal is for the two teams to second-guess what the viewers will vote for in various questions by using an app and voting along live.

evidence.title: Micro Men
evidence.text: Micro Men, working title Syntax Era is a one-off BBC drama television show set in the late 1970s and the early-mid 1980s, about the rise of the British home computer market.

evidence.title: Micro Men
evidence.text: It focuses on the rivalry between Sir Clive Sinclair (played by Alexander Armstrong), who developed the ZX Spectrum, and Chris Curry (played by Martin Freeman), the man behind the BBC Micro.

evidence.title: Pointless
evidence.text: Pointless is a British quiz show produced by Endemol UK for the BBC, hosted by Alexander Armstrong and Richard Osman.

evidence.title: Pointless
evidence.text: Each episode of the quiz features teams of two contestants attempting to find correct but obscure answers to general knowledge questions in order to score as few points as possible, and become eligible to compete for the show's cash jackpot.

evidence.title: Pointless
evidence.text: All questions used on the show are factual in nature, and are asked to a panel of 100 individuals in a pre-conducted public survey.

evidence.title: Pointless
evidence.text: Contestants seek to find correct answers that were given by as few participants as possible; those given by no participants are termed "pointless" and are the most desirable.

evidence.title: Pointless
evidence.text: Every pointless answer given during the main game increases the jackpot by £250, and one such answer must be given in the final round in order to win it.

evidence.title: Combat Jack
evidence.text: Reggie Ossé, also known as Combat Jack (born July 8, 1969 in Brooklyn, New York) is a former hip hop music attorney and executive, and also the former managing editor of "The Source".

evidence.title: Combat Jack
evidence.text: He is the host of the podcast "The Combat Jack Show" and founding partner of the Loud Speakers Podcast network.

evidence.title: Combat Jack
evidence.text: He was also the host of the Complex TV show version of the Combat Jack Show podcast.

evidence.title: Ben Miller
evidence.text: Bennet Evan "Ben" Miller (born 24 February 1966) is an English comedian, actor and director.

evidence.title: Ben Miller
evidence.text: He is best known as one half of comedy double act Armstrong and Miller, with Alexander Armstrong.

evidence.title: Ben Miller
evidence.text: Miller and Armstrong wrote and starred in the Channel 4 sketch show "Armstrong and Miller", as well as the BBC sketch show "The Armstrong & Miller Show".

evidence.title: Ben Miller
evidence.text: Miller is also known for playing the lead role of DI Richard Poole in the first 2 series of the BBC Crime Drama "Death in Paradise".
